intended_object: The Boolean edge-coordinate vector (edge indicator on unordered pairs {i,j} of distinct naturals) of a finite simple graph H on {0,…,n−1}, with H seen as a graph on ℕ through the inclusion Fin n ↪ ℕ. Inferred from the docstring and from how the file and Infinite/Basic.lean use it.
explanation: The body pushes H forward along the inclusion `Fin.valEmbedding : Fin n ↪ ℕ`, which gives a graph on ℕ whose only edges are those of H, relabelled into ℕ. It then applies `graphCoordEquiv`, which sends a graph G on ℕ to e ↦ [e ∈ G.edgeSet], for e ranging over the unordered pairs of distinct naturals (`EdgeIndex`). So coordinate {i,j} is true exactly when i,j < n and the pair is adjacent in H. This is the edge indicator vector the docstring describes. The lemma `graphCoordEquiv_eq_windowCoord` confirms the intended behaviour: inside the window, the coordinates of a graph on ℕ agree with the window coordinates of its restriction to the first n vertices. Generality is not an issue: the construction is tied to the library's fixed coordinate space on ℕ, and `Fin n` is exactly the setting of the finite windows. Mathlib has no matching declaration. This is mostly a convenience helper for the projective-limit argument, but it is a well-defined, correctly implemented mathematical object.
